milestones.title: Section 1.1 (Kutz): the Devil defeats the king
milestones.milestone_description: Kutz (2004), Chapter 1, Section 1.1, pp. 2–3, describes Berlekamp's king-capture result. In the shared infinite-board game, there exists one ordinary Devil strategy D such that every power-one Angel strategy A fails to survive. The formal statement is existential in D before universal in A. No optimal capture time or illustrated board-size bound is asserted.

milestones.title: Theorem 2.7: reduction to a Nice Devil
milestones.milestone_description: For every positive integer power, if the Angel has no winning strategy, some Nice Devil can keep every finite safe play in a fixed box of positive integer radius. This formulation includes the determinacy observation from the introduction in addition to Theorem 2.7.

milestones.title: Theorem 4.5: power two escapes every Nice Devil
milestones.milestone_description: There exists one power-two Angel strategy that survives against every Nice Devil and, against each such opponent, reaches outside every finite box centred at the origin.

milestones.title: Theorem 4.6 (Mathe): the Angel of power two wins
milestones.milestone_description: Mathe (2007), Theorem 4.6: the Angel of power 2 wins. There exists a single power-two Angel strategy surviving forever against every ordinary Devil strategy on the infinite integer lattice, with the shared Devil-first and passing conventions. This is the original mission goal, retained as a source milestone under the complete classification.
